To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the prospects for dark matter detection by GLAST in the Galactic center are very promising, and the prospects for PAMELA in the Galactic halo are poor, and (ii) the most probable values of the fluxes are strongly dependent on the priors.
the prospects of detecting a signal of neutralino dark matter are very good, but that they strongly depend on the details of the dark matter halo and propagation models.
the most probable diffuse gamma radiation flux is in the range of 10-8-10-7 GeV cm-2 s-1 sr-1, and the most probable positron flux is in the region below 10-5 GeV cm-3 s-1 sr.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prospects of detecting the diffuse gamma radiation and positron flux from dark matter annihilation in the Galaxy.
the statistical analysis of the prospects of indirect detection of dark matter in the Constrained Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model.
the question of how to interpret the results of dark matter searches in terms of the MSSM parameter space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the prospects of indirect detection of neutralino dark matter in the Constrained MSMM are very poor, and that, even in the best-case scenario, GLAST would be able to detect only a very tiny fraction of the MSSM parameter space, while PAMELA would not be able to detect any signal.
, in the Constrained Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, dark matter indirect detection experiments are unlikely to provide a decisive test for supersymmetry.

the prospects for indirect detection of dark matter in the Constrained (and in the MSSM in general) are rather poor, at least for the present generation of detectors and with the present understanding of the propagation of cosmic rays in the Galaxy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Constrained MSSMs are in general difficult to probe by indirect detection, and that a positive signal should be taken with a grain of salt.
the prospects of dark matter indirect detection are rather poor in the MSSM, at least in the context of the Constrained MSSMs.
there is no reason to expect that the GLAST and PAMELA experiments will be able to detect the neutralino annihilation signal, unless the halo profile is very cuspy and the boost factor is very large.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of any additional information on the halo model and on the propagation parameters, the prospects for dark matter detection by indirect methods are rather bleak.

, in the Constrained and other phenomenologically viable supersymmetric models, the diffuse gamma radiation and positron fluxes due to neutralino annihilation are highly model dependent, with a large spread in the predictions.
the Constrained MSSMs are not in conflict with the current experimental data on dark matter indirect detection.
